Navigating Florida Homeowners Insurance Rates in 2026

May 11, 2026 · HOInsurance.com

Greetings from your trusted Florida insurance agent since 1966! As we navigate 2026, many of you are understandably concerned about the fluctuating landscape of Florida homeowners insurance rates. It’s a complex issue, but understanding the key drivers can help you make informed decisions for your most valuable asset.

Why Are Florida Home Insurance Rates So High?

Florida's unique geography and climate unfortunately place it at a higher risk for natural disasters. Hurricanes, tropical storms, and even severe thunderstorms contribute significantly to insurance claims. Additionally, the rising cost of reinsurance (insurance for insurance companies) and a litigious environment in the state have put upward pressure on premiums. For example, Florida accounted for 79% of all homeowners insurance lawsuits nationwide in 2021, despite making up only 9% of the country’s homeowners claims. This disproportionate legal activity directly impacts what you pay.

Factors Influencing Your Specific Premium

While statewide trends are important, your individual premium is shaped by several factors:

  • Home's Age and Construction: Older homes, especially those not up to current building codes, often face higher premiums. Wind mitigation features like hurricane-resistant windows or a strong roof-to-wall attachment can significantly reduce your cost.
  • Location: Proximity to the coast or flood zones (which also impacts your Florida flood insurance rates) will always be a major factor.
  • Claims History: A history of claims, even small ones, can increase your rates.
  • Deductibles: Opting for a higher deductible can lower your annual premium, but ensure you can comfortably cover that amount if a claim arises.
